strategy_title: evict_first + Contiguity Hints on Strided Load Causes Regression
strategy_description: Applying evict_first eviction policy to a large strided tensor load (combined with incorrect tl.max_contiguous/tl.multiple_of hints where the hint value 64 exceeds the actual tile size YBLOCK=8) caused L2 hit rate to drop from 58.86% to 48.02%, warp cycles per issued instruction to increase from 29.4 to 44.5, and kernel duration to increase from 1.62ms to 2.42ms (0.67x regression). Despite the tensor far exceeding L2 capacity, the kernel's 249 waves/SM creates inter-block data reuse that the L2 was servicing; evict_first destroyed this reuse. The incorrect contiguity hints (tl.multiple_of with N > tile_size) may additionally cause compiler misoptimization by asserting a false memory layout contract.
slow_pseudocode:
# AFTER (regressed) - evict_first + wrong contiguity hints
y0 = tl.max_contiguous(tl.multiple_of((yindex % 64), [64, 1]), [64, 1])  # YBLOCK=8 < 64: hint is WRONG
tmp0 = tl.load(in_ptr0 + (y0 + 64*x2 + 16842816*y1), mask=xmask & ymask, eviction_policy='evict_first')
tmp1 = tl.load(in_ptr1 + (y0), mask=ymask, eviction_policy='evict_last')
tmp3 = tl.load(in_ptr2 + (y0), mask=ymask, eviction_policy='evict_last')
fast_pseudocode:
# BEFORE (baseline) - evict_last, no contiguity hints
y0 = (yindex % 64)
tmp0 = tl.load(in_ptr0 + (y0 + 64*x2 + 16842816*y1), mask=ymask & xmask, eviction_policy='evict_last')
tmp1 = tl.load(in_ptr1 + (y0), mask=ymask, eviction_policy='evict_last')
tmp3 = tl.load(in_ptr2 + (y0), mask=ymask, eviction_policy='evict_last')
applicable_when: Never — this combination of evict_first on a large tensor with high wave count and incorrect contiguity hints consistently causes regression
do_not_apply_when: When the kernel has very high waves/SM (>100) and the tensor, though larger than L2 capacity, has inter-block data reuse that benefits from L2 caching (L2 hit rate >40%). When tl.multiple_of hint value N exceeds the actual tile size for that dimension, the hint is incorrect and must not be used. Do not apply evict_first to tensors where L2 hit rate is already meaningful (>40%) — the cache is providing real reuse even for tensors larger than L2 capacity.
framework_notes: In Triton, tl.multiple_of(x, N) asserts that x is always a multiple of N. If tile_size < N, the modulo result (yindex % N) within a tile will NOT be a multiple of N for most tiles, making the hint incorrect. tl.max_contiguous(x, N) asserts N consecutive values are contiguous — also invalid when tile size < N. Incorrect contiguity hints can cause the compiler to emit wrong vectorized instructions. This is the second iteration confirming this regression pattern (iter 3 speedup=0.6763, iter 4 speedup=0.6736).

This generates ~100M non-fused FP32 instructions that cannot be pipelined with FMA units, directly causing the IssueSlotUtilization bottleneck (only 35% of cycles issue an instruction). All prior attempts (coalescing, autotune, flat-1D) failed due to harness crashes or correctness issues — this approach requires no tile/grid changes and is purely a compute-path substitution, making it safe and minimal.
